name: First-hour afternoon filter
tagline: Overnight drift plus a first-hour gate for the afternoon, under a 165-day QQQ regime.
summary: Hold TQQQ overnight (15:59 to 09:31) and through the first hour while QQQ is above its 165-day SMA. At 10:29 compute the QQQ first-hour return; hold TQQQ for the afternoon only if it is non-negative, otherwise move to cash at the 10:30 open and re-enter at 15:59. Risk-off days are 100% BIL.
decision_process: Each session: (1) the 165-day SMA regime uses QQQ's prior close; risk-off means 100% BIL. (2) On risk-on days, enter TQQQ at the 15:59 open (decision on the 15:58 QQQ close vs the SMA through the prior day) and hold through the next 09:31 open. (3) Hold through the first hour. (4) At the 10:29 close compute r60 = QQQ close(10:29) / QQQ open(09:30) - 1; if r60 >= 0 hold TQQQ to the 15:59 open, else sell at the 10:30 open and hold cash until the 15:59 open, then re-enter for the overnight. All signals use only data through the decision bar; all fills are at the next bar's open.
rules: Regime: QQQ close(t-1) > 165-day SMA of QQQ closes through t-1 -> risk-on; otherwise 100% BIL.
Risk-on: hold TQQQ from the 15:59 open through the next 09:31 open (overnight) and through the first hour.
At 10:29 compute r60 = QQQ close(10:29) / QQQ open(09:30) - 1.
If r60 >= 0, hold TQQQ from the 10:30 open to the 15:59 open; if r60 < 0, sell at the 10:30 open, hold cash until the 15:59 open, then re-enter TQQQ for the overnight.
Long-only, weights <= 100%; 1 bp per side primary, 5 bp sensitivity; 2% band; no look-ahead.
verdict: Passes vs TQQQ at 1 bp and 5 bp on both windows, and beats the daily baseline on all four metrics at 1 bp (10y 55.63%/44.89%, 5y 46.36%/32.64%). At 5 bp the 10y CAGR is 43.46%, 1.85 pp below the baseline's 1 bp figure and about 0.7 pp below the baseline's own 5 bp figure, so this is not a clean win at realistic costs. The max drawdown is the COVID crash (-44.6%), and the first-hour signal is statistically weak (t ~1.4-2.3).

sources.idea: The first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour return (market intraday momentum).
sources.source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018) / Market Intraday Momentum, JFE 129(2)
sources.evidence: Documents the first-half-hour -> last-half-hour effect in SPY 1993-2013 and ten other ETFs, stronger on volatile, high-volume and macro-news days. We tested the mechanism directly: the last-30-minute version does not replicate in QQQ/TQQQ 2016-2026, but the broader first-hour -> afternoon version does (see rejected_sources for the failed last-30m version).

sources.idea: Intraday momentum is driven by gamma hedging from option dealers and leveraged ETFs; the rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 minutes.
sources.source: Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (2021) / Hedging Demand and Market Intraday Momentum, JFE 142(1)
sources.evidence: Documents intraday momentum across 60+ futures (1974-2020) and links it to hedging demand from market makers and leveraged ETFs. This is the economic rationale for using the first-hour signal to time the TQQQ afternoon and for expecting the effect to be concentrated around leveraged-ETF rebalancing.

sources.idea: Strategy premia accrue either overnight or intraday; momentum-type premia are earned overnight.
sources.source: Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019) / A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns, JFE 134(1)
sources.evidence: Documents the overnight/intraday decomposition and the persistence of overnight premia. Our own QQQ/TQQQ decomposition agrees: TQQQ earns 30.2%/yr overnight vs 5.9%/yr intraday (2016-2026), which is why the strategy keeps the overnight leg and why pure intraday timing fails.

sources.idea: Daily re-leveraging of 3x ETFs creates path dependence and end-of-day rebalancing flows.
sources.source: Cheng & Madhavan (2009) / The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds, JOIM
sources.evidence: Explains the daily reset/path dependence of TQQQ and the mechanical end-of-day hedging flows. Used to motivate the leveraged-ETF channel and the caveat that TQQQ's realized path and future rebalancing flows may differ from a simple 3x overlay.

sources.idea: Use a 165-day SMA on QQQ as the risk-on/risk-off gate; use cash (not BIL) for the afternoon exit.
sources.source: Own test / no external source (project daily baseline)
sources.evidence: The 165-day SMA is the project's pre-existing daily baseline (README: 45.31%/58.71% 10y, 34.61%/36.86% 5y). We inherited the parameter rather than fitting it. Cash-vs-BIL for the afternoon exit was chosen by direct comparison: cash improved 10y CAGR by 2.9 pp at 1 bp and 13.2 pp at 5 bp.

sources.idea: Overnight drift: US equity returns are concentrated in the close-to-open period.
sources.source: Haghani, Ragulin & Dewey / Night Moves: Overnight Drift (Elm Wealth)
sources.evidence: The current web page lists this as a supporting paper. It documents the overnight drift, consistent with our own decomposition (TQQQ 30.2%/yr overnight vs 5.9%/yr intraday). It was not used to set the rule and is not cited in the original report; keep it only as a supporting reference.

rejected_sources.source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018) / last-half-hour timing version
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Tested directly and it does not replicate in QQQ/TQQQ 2016-2026: TQQQ's last-30-minute return after a positive first 30m is -1.60 bp/day on the 10y window and -2.43 bp/day on the 5y window. The predictability is in the midday/afternoon (+17.1 bp/day for TQQQ 10:00-15:30 after a positive first 30m on 10y), not in the close, so the strategy holds the afternoon rather than only the last 30 minutes.

rejected_sources.source: Own test / no external source - pure intraday 30m and 60m variants (P1, P2)
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Long TQQQ only from 10:00/10:30 to the close on a positive first-30/60m signal, flat overnight, earns 12.89%/8.96% CAGR on the 10y window (10.80%/32.26% on 5y after 1 bp costs). TQQQ's drift is mostly overnight (30.2%/yr vs 5.9%/yr intraday), so pure intraday timing cannot reach TQQQ's 39.28%/13.47%.

rejected_sources.source: Own test / no external source - overnight-only + 165-day SMA (P4)
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Overnight-only earns 27.66%/47.18% on 10y and 14.42%/34.69% on 5y; it passes the 5y TQQQ test but fails the 10y CAGR (27.66% < 39.28%). It also loses -8.46%/yr at 5 bp because of the daily round trips. The first-hour afternoon sleeve is needed for the 10y.

rejected_sources.source: Own test / no external source - afternoon exit to BIL instead of cash
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Exiting to BIL doubles the fills (two legs each way) and lowered 10y CAGR from 55.63% to 52.71% at 1 bp and from 43.46% to 30.25% at 5 bp. Cash was kept for the intraday exit; BIL is still used for the multi-day risk-off regime.

corrections: Rule text ambiguity: the current page says 'Hold TQQQ from 15:59 to 10:30'. This is only the overnight + first-hour leg. After 10:30 the position is held to 15:59 only if r60 >= 0; if r60 < 0 it is sold at the 10:30 open and re-entered at 15:59. The rule list should say this explicitly.

Missing 5 bp metrics: the page shows only the 1 bp figures. Add 10y 43.46% CAGR / 46.90% DD and 5y 35.80% CAGR / 34.50% DD. At 5 bp the 10y CAGR is 1.85 pp below the baseline's 1 bp figure and about 0.7 pp below the baseline's own 5 bp figure, while the DD is 11.8 pp lower.

Name: 'First-hour momentum' overstates the intraday component. The edge is a hybrid: the overnight drift is the main return source and the first-hour signal only gates the afternoon. A more accurate display name is 'First-hour afternoon filter' or 'Overnight + first-hour filter'.

Drawdown convention: the page's 44.89% (10y) and 32.64% (5y) are minute-mark drawdowns; the daily-close marks are 44.59% and 30.37%. The TQQQ 81.68% benchmark is a daily-close figure, so state the convention or show both for comparability.

Paper list: the page includes Elm Wealth's 'Night Moves: Overnight Drift', which is not cited in the original report. Either keep it explicitly as a supporting reference for the overnight drift (medium confidence) or remove it; do not present it as the source of the rule.

Verdict is one-sided: it says 'Fails the daily baseline at 5 bp on the 10y' but does not say that it beats the daily baseline on all four metrics at 1 bp. Add the 1 bp comparison so the reader sees both sides.

Report wording (also applies to the report, not only the page): the 5 bp comparison quotes the baseline's 1 bp CAGR (45.31%). The fair 5 bp comparison is 43.46% vs about 44.2% (roughly a 0.7 pp gap), so the report should label which cost assumption each number uses.
